boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-admission outdoor hangs at named Winooski Valley Park District destinations near Saint Michael’s College.

cards.title: Walk the Colchester Pond loop
cards.subtitle: Colchester
cards.notes: Bring a friend for the 3.5-mile pond loop, pausing at the water and picnic areas; pack out everything you bring.
cards.short_summary: A forest-and-pond walking loop with wildlife-viewing opportunities.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Colchester Pond Natural Area as a 182-acre park with a 3.5-mile walking trail, picnic areas, and wildlife viewing; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; follow posted park rules.

cards.title: Meet at Delta Park’s river mouth
cards.subtitle: Colchester
cards.notes: Take a daytime walk along the natural sandy shoreline and look across the Winooski River; stay mindful of changing water conditions.
cards.short_summary: A riverside park with sandy shoreline and varied ecosystems.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Delta Park as a 55-acre park at the mouth of the Winooski River with natural sandy beaches; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; follow posted park rules and shoreline guidance.

cards.title: Hike Macrae Farm Park
cards.subtitle: Colchester
cards.notes: Choose a hiking or cross-country trail, set an easy turnaround point, and keep the group together through meadow and forest sections.
cards.short_summary: A large Colchester park with meadow, floodplain, and hardwood-forest trails.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Macrae Farm Park as a 288-acre park offering hiking and cross-country trails; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; check trail conditions before heading out.

cards.title: Look for habitats at Wolcott Family Natural Area
cards.subtitle: Colchester
cards.notes: Walk the developing one-mile loop and use the viewing areas to notice marsh and Pond Brook habitats without leaving marked routes.
cards.short_summary: A Colchester natural area with marsh, riparian habitat, and a planned loop trail.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Wolcott Family Natural Area as a 61.7-acre park with marsh and riparian habitats, a one-mile loop trail, and viewing areas; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; use established trails and viewing areas.

cards.title: Take the Woodside loop
cards.subtitle: Essex, connected to Saint Michael’s Natural Area trail
cards.notes: Follow the 1.5-mile loop with friends for river and wetland views, then return before dusk using the marked route.
cards.short_summary: A loop trail through forest and beaver-influenced wetland near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Woodside Natural Area as having a 1.5-mile loop trail with Winooski River and wetland views; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; Saint Michael’s notes its Natural Area trail connects to Woodside.

cards.title: Walk the Ethan Allen Homestead Park trails
cards.subtitle: Burlington
cards.notes: Use the boardwalk and river trails for a relaxed group walk; this card covers the park, not the separate paid museum tour.
cards.short_summary: A riverside park with floodplain-forest trails and a cattail-marsh boardwalk.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Ethan Allen Homestead as a 284-acre park with trails and an elevated cattail-marsh boardwalk; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD park access is free from dawn to dusk. The separately operated Ethan Allen Homestead Museum is not included.

cards.title: Picnic at Mayes Landing
cards.subtitle: Burlington, beside the Burlington Bike Path
cards.notes: Claim a picnic table for conversation and river watching, then stroll the nearby path; bring your own food or simply sit together.
cards.short_summary: A shaded grassy riverfront stop with picnic tables by the bike path.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Mayes Landing as a grassy area with picnic tables beside the Burlington Bike Path near the Winooski River mouth; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; no purchase is needed to use the picnic area.

cards.title: Follow the Riverwalk Trail
cards.subtitle: Burlington–Winooski border
cards.notes: Walk the half-mile river route with a friend and pause safely at designated overlooks near the falls; avoid slippery rocks and strong water.
cards.short_summary: A short named riverwalk beside the Winooski River Falls.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Salmon Hole Park and Riverwalk Trail as a park at the Winooski River Falls with a roughly half-mile trail; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; keep clear of hazardous river edges and follow posted rules.

cards.title: Explore Derway Island Nature Preserve
cards.subtitle: Burlington
cards.notes: Make this a quiet nature walk: move slowly, watch for floodplain plants and wildlife, and leave the preserve as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A large Winooski River floodplain nature preserve for low-key exploration.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Derway Island Nature Preserve as a 148-acre preserve along the Winooski River with floodplain ecosystems; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; observe wildlife without disturbing habitat.

cards.title: See the Donahue Sea Caves landscape
cards.subtitle: Burlington
cards.notes: Visit in daylight to view the cattail marsh and ancient limestone-dolomite cave features from safe, permitted areas; do not enter unstable spaces.
cards.short_summary: A small park with cattail marsh and documented ancient cave formations.
cards.evidence_claim: WVPD identifies Donahue Sea Caves as a 15-acre park with cattail marsh and ancient limestone-dolomite caves; its parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: WVPD parks are open to the public free of charge from dawn to dusk; respect barriers, habitat, and any site-specific warnings.
